text: In the deep sea, a male anglerfish bites a female, and never lets go.
Down there, it's pitch black, and partners are hard to find.
The males are tiny. In extreme cases, females are more than sixty times longer.
So when a male finds one, he bites her.
Then their skin and blood vessels fuse. He becomes part of her body.
He can even lose his eyes and fins. She supplies everything.
But wait. Bodies reject foreign tissue. So why doesn't hers?
In 2020, scientists studied the DNA of anglerfish species.
They found these fish have lost key parts of the immune system, the parts that would attack a transplant.
For humans, losing those would be fatal.
Verdict: true. Permanent fusion, made possible by a rewired immune system.
